subject: Biology
title: Classifying Microorganisms
description: Learn Classifying Microorganisms in one minute.

hook.text: Microbes are wildly diverse. Sorting them into groups took centuries of debate.

buildup.text: The three domains of life are Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya. Two of those are entirely microbial.

discovery.text: Carl Woese used ribosomal RNA to reclassify life, revealing Archaea as a separate domain in 1977.

twist.text: Archaea look like bacteria under a microscope but are genetically closer to us.

climax.text: Modern genomics keeps reshuffling the microbial family tree as new species are discovered.

punchline.text: The tree of life keeps growing new branches.

quiz.question: Who used ribosomal RNA to discover the domain Archaea?

details.summary: Microorganisms are classified into bacteria, archaea, fungi, protists, and viruses based on cellular structure, genetics, and metabolism. Modern molecular taxonomy using ribosomal RNA sequencing has revolutionized classification, revealing that the microbial tree of life is far more diverse than...
details.whyItMatters: Accurate classification is essential for identifying pathogens, developing treatments, and understanding microbial ecology. Molecular methods have discovered entirely new groups of microbes that cannot be cultured in the laboratory.
takeaways: The three domains of life are Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya
16S ribosomal RNA sequencing revolutionized microbial classification
Over 99 percent of microbial species cannot be grown in laboratory culture

faq.question: Why can most microbes not be cultured in the lab?
faq.answer: Most microbes depend on specific nutrients, temperatures, oxygen levels, or symbiotic partners that are difficult to replicate artificially. They may require chemical signals from neighboring species. Metagenomics now identifies them directly from environmental DNA.

faq.question: How did molecular methods change microbial classification?
faq.answer: Before molecular tools, classification relied on appearance and biochemistry, which missed deep evolutionary relationships. Ribosomal RNA comparison revealed that Archaea are as different from Bacteria as both are from Eukarya, creating the three-domain system.
